Crates (b. 400 BCE, Olynthus) was a religious figure or clergy of the Classical era, an age of empires, philosophical inquiry, and foundational civilizations, active in Olynthus. Known in the fields of architects & engineers.

Crates was a prominent figure in Olynthus, a city-state in ancient Greece, and played a significant role in the development of its architectural and engineering prowess. His contributions to the field of architecture were notable, particularly in the design of public buildings and temples. Crates was also known for his expertise in the management of public works and infrastructure projects.

Crates' legacy can be seen in the many architectural and engineering achievements of Olynthus, which were influenced by his innovative designs and management techniques. The city's impressive collection of public buildings, including temples, theaters, and public baths, was a testament to Crates' skill and expertise. Crates' work also had a lasting impact on the development of engineering techniques in ancient Greece.

Crates was a key figure in the cultural and intellectual landscape of Olynthus, and his contributions to the field of architecture and engineering had a profound impact on the city's growth and prosperity. His legacy continues to be felt today, and he remains an important figure in the history of ancient Greek architecture and engineering.

The significance of Crates' work can be seen in the many examples of his innovative designs and management techniques that have been preserved in historical records. His work had a lasting impact on the development of architecture and engineering in ancient Greece, and his legacy continues to inspire architects and engineers to this day.
